stories.headline: U2 Is Bringing the Greatest Show on Earth to Our Stadiums
stories.blurb: Fresh off Carnaval De Luz, their first album of new songs in nine years, U2 just announced 15 North American stadium shows running August to October next year. Stephen Wilson Jr. opens the first nine dates and the War On Drugs take the last six. Can't wait that long? The band plays halftime of tonight's Thanksgiving Eve game between the Rams and the Packers, live on Netflix.
stories.quip: Bono in a stadium with a light show is basically a holiday tradition at this point.

stories.headline: 39 Million People Have Already Visited Vice City on PlayStation
stories.blurb: Sony says more than 39 million unique players have fired up GTA 6 on PlayStation, and it now holds the record for most concurrent players ever on the platform. Players have logged 683 million hours so far, about 17.4 hours each. It was also the first game played on 70 percent of brand-new PS5s.
stories.quip: 683 million hours, and at least half of them were spent picking outfits.

stories.headline: Stray Kids Asked for a Metal Cover. Instagram Delivered.
stories.blurb: In an interview with Consequence, Stray Kids said they'd love to hear My Chemical Romance, Yungblud or Metallica cover their songs. Madrid musician Sergio Moreno took that as a challenge and posted a heavy version of "RUN IT" mashing all three styles together. It's pulled in about 400,000 views and 70,000 likes on Instagram so far.
stories.quip: Somewhere James Hetfield just felt a sudden urge to learn a K-pop dance.

stories.headline: Mario Kart World Just Got Eight Free Remixed Tracks
stories.blurb: Nintendo's Version 1.9.0 update adds eight new courses to Mario Kart World, each a remix of an existing track, like Airship Fortress 2, Koopa Troopa Beach 2 and Shy Guy Bazaar 2. Knockout Tour gets two new routes called Feather Rally and Lucky Cat Rally. Your latest races and battles now save automatically as replays, and confetti falls on the results screen.
stories.quip: Finally, video proof of that blue shell injustice.

stories.headline: Fans Gave Wind Waker the PC and Mac Glow-Up It Deserves
stories.blurb: A fan project called Wind Waker Recomp lets The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker run natively on Windows and Apple Silicon Macs. It adds widescreen, mouse and keyboard support, and frame rates up to 240 FPS instead of the usual 30. You can even toggle on Wii U-style upgrades like the Swift Sail. You'll need your own copy of the game, since the files aren't included.
stories.quip: Toon Link at 240 FPS is the smoothest sailor on the Great Sea.

stories.headline: Lego Jeff the Land Shark Swims Out of Marvel Rivals
stories.blurb: Marvel Rivals is getting its very first Lego set, and of course it's Jeff the Land Shark. The kit has just under 500 pieces, stands about 5 inches tall and 8.5 inches long, and his mouth, legs, tongue and tail all move. He lands on shelves January 1, 2027.
stories.quip: He's a good boy. He's a shark. He's now 500 tiny plastic bricks.

stories.headline: Focker-in-Law Opens Today, and Ariana Grande Joins the Circle of Trust
stories.blurb: The fourth movie in the Meet the Parents franchise hits theaters today, 16 years after the last one. Robert De Niro, Ben Stiller and Owen Wilson are back, and this time Greg's son Henry (Skyler Gisondo) brings home his girlfriend, an FBI hostage negotiator played by Ariana Grande. Perfect timing for a family-chaos comedy right before Thanksgiving.
stories.quip: Jack Byrnes versus a trained hostage negotiator. Grab the popcorn and the lie detector.

stories.headline: A Top Tokyo Udon Shop Is Slurping Its Way to Flatiron
stories.blurb: Udon Shin, a Shibuya favorite since 2011 and one of the top-rated udon spots in Tokyo, opens at 37 W. 17th Street on Saturday, December 19. The noodles are made fresh on site with flour from Japan, and the signature dish is udon carbonara. It's walk-ins only, with room for about 60 to 70 people.
stories.quip: Carbonara udon is the crossover episode we didn't know we needed.

stories.headline: Incoming! An Alaska Pilot Bombs Remote Families With Turkeys
stories.blurb: Every Thanksgiving, pilot Esther Keim flies her single-engine plane over Skwentna, Alaska, a tiny village with no roads or grocery stores, and drops frozen turkeys to families below. She revived the tradition from Kenny Hughes, a pilot she watched do it when she was a kid. Volunteers sew burlap sacks tied with bright yellow tape so the turkeys are easy to spot in the snow.
stories.quip: The only acceptable kind of bird strike.

stories.headline: Town Cat Gets a Bronze Statue, Skips Her Own Unveiling
stories.blurb: Susie the cat is a local celebrity in Dorchester, England, famous for wandering into the town's pubs, shops and supermarkets. On November 23, crowds gathered to unveil a bronze statue of her wearing Roman-style beads, a nod to the town's ancient history. Susie did not attend. She was busy checking out a local supermarket instead.
stories.quip: Fame never changed her. She still has errands to run.
